newsitem.title: USA: Telebras falls on court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Telebras falls on court ruling.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Brazilian telecommunications holding Telebras SA fell on Wednesday on news Brazil's Supreme Court had approved pay raises for 11 civil servants, traders said.

Telebras was off 2-1/2 to 95-1/8 in late afternoon on heavy volume of almost 2.2 million shares. The ADRs had hit a year high of about 99-1/2 at midday, bolstered by comments about privatization of the company from Brazil's communications minister.
Traders said the ADRs fell after the high court voted in favor of a 28.9 percent pay raise for 11 civil servants who had sued to get the same raise as the armed forces did in 1993.
Brazil's reformist government fears that a favorable ruling could set a precedent for the entire federal workforce and cost billions of dollars in extra pay.
Telebras ADRs have risen from about 75 at the start of the year, boosted by privatization plans, inexpensive valuation and earnings.
